newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says veterinary talks with U.S. progress.
newsitem.headline: EU says veterinary talks with U.S. progress.

text.p: Talks with the United States on veterinary standards affecting trans-Atlantic trade are well advanced and may be resolved by late February, a European Commission spokesman said on Monday.
An agreement was signed with New Zealand last month and another has effectively been reached with the Czech Republic.

A package of agreements on mutual recognition of standards is expected to be concluded soon afterwards between the European Union and Australia, Canada and several South American and eastern European countries.
Commenting on the talks, EU Farm Commisioner Franz Fischler said at a news conference after a meeting of EU farm ministers that only technical matters were delaying agreement with the United States.
In December, the two sides agreed to extend current arrangments to April to allow time for the talks to be concluded.
The U.S. has placed great importance on the pet food sector.
"Progress is being made and the problems that still remain are technical dossiers which we believe can be resolved," Fischler said.

He added that the EU was determined to ensure that the standards which will be adopted will be those of the EU, notably the principle of regionalisation under which measures can be applied on a regional, instead of national, basis.
